Skip a spouse who's already in the blood-relative set (e.g. cousin marriage) to avoid double-counting. This whole walk is bounded by the project's own connectivity, cheap for a typical project. For a very large/broadly-connected file where the walk itself gets expensive, an alternative is scanning every Individual once and computing each one's relation to the start point via fhCallBuiltInFunction("Relationship"/"RelationCode", startPtr, ptr, ...) instead (see fhCallBuiltInFunction.htm) -- trades a bounded graph walk for one built-in call per Individual in the project; which is actually cheaper is a judgement call based on file size and connectivity, not a fixed rule.

title: "Did they move between birth and death?": PLAC>LATLONG distance beats parsing county/country out of free text
breadcrumb: Detecting a move via lat/long distance
source: user suggestion, issue #63, refining an earlier PLAC-text-parsing caveat -- verified live against Family Historian Sample Project 8: 12/111 Individuals have BIRT/DEAT PLAC>LATLONG coordinates over 15 miles apart (one pair 4,347 miles, clearly transatlantic), 94/111 lack coordinates for one or both ends (mostly no DEAT fact recorded at all)
text: For "did this person move between birth and death" (or between any two facts), a haversine distance between each fact's PLAC>LATLONG:LAT_NUMERIC/LONG_NUMERIC coordinates (see data-reference-qualifiers-place-latlong) is a cleaner signal than trying to parse a county or country out of the PLAC field's free text (see run-lua-guidance-family-query-helpers-adjacent caveats on PLAC:SHORT/MEDIUM being ambiguous between a 2-part "Town, Country" and a 3-part "Town, County, Country" place string) -- coordinates don't have that ambiguity, and every _PLAC record already carries them (see the Place and lat/long qualifiers entry). Pick a distance threshold appropriate to what "moved" should mean (a few miles is noise/imprecise geocoding of the same town; tens of miles is a real move) rather than a fixed universal cutoff. This only tells you THAT they moved and how far, not a place name for where to/from -- if a human-readable place (a county or country name specifically) is actually wanted, fall back to text parsing: read the place string from its END backward (the last comma-separated segment is normally the country, the second-to-last the county, per how UK/Commonwealth place hierarchies are conventionally entered), and when the last segment doesn't look like a recognizable country at all, that's the case to ask the user directly rather than guess -- don't silently assume a country when the source data doesn't actually name one.

title: run_lua guidance: never combine a write with its own verification in the same script
source: 2026-08-06 grilling session on issue #65, root-caused against the reporter's own failing script
text: Always do a write and the read-only script that verifies it as two separate run_lua calls, never both in one script. docs/adr/0005's write tracker (sandbox.lua) only re-raises a script's error (the mechanism that gives FH's own auto-undo a chance to fire — see writeSessionRolledBack) when THAT SAME SCRIPT itself called a tracked write primitive before erroring; a script with zero tracked writes behaves exactly like Read-only on error, no rollback risk at all. Combining a write with trailing verification reads in one script defeats this protection even though the verification reads are themselves harmless: if the write half succeeds and the verification half then crashes on an unrelated bug (e.g. a bad id), the tracker is already true from the write half, so the crash still triggers a full rollback of everything written across the whole Session, not just this call — confirmed empirically (issue #65): a script that called fhBridge.logActivity three times (real writes) and then crashed on fhBridge.getFactsByTag(136, "BIRT") (a plain-number id, not "I136" — see run-lua-guidance-call-shape-gotchas' sibling entries on qualified ids) rolled back three sources, three citations, three facts, and a date correction from earlier, separate, already-succeeded run_lua calls in the same Session. Keep verification reads in their own call after the write call has already returned successfully — a bug in that later, read-only call then has nothing for the tracker to have already flagged, and fails harmlessly.

title: run_lua guidance: transcribing a tabular source (e.g. a GRO certificate) means building a real FTF <table>, not bullet-separated header/data lines
source: user correction, issue #71 (and the related fhGetItemText truncation bug, issue #70): a Claude session transcribed a GRO birth/marriage certificate's field grid (source S1462/S1463/S1464, template T22 "Civil Registration Certificate") into a Source's TEXT field as two •-separated plain-text lines (a header line, then a matching data line) instead of a real FTF table. Two other sources using the exact same template (S1411, S1416) do use correct <table="w|w|...">/<row>...|...|...</row> markup, but the user confirmed (issue #71 comment) those two were entered by hand -- via FH's own UI, not run_lua -- so they are NOT evidence that any Claude session has already produced a real FTF table for a tabular source transcription. As far as this project's history shows, every Claude-authored transcription of a tabular source has used the •-flattened form; this entry exists to change that going forward, not because a prior session already knew the right approach and another one regressed.
text: When transcribing a source whose original layout is genuinely tabular (a GRO/civil registration certificate's field grid, a census return's household rows, any source with real rows and columns), write it into the TEXT field as an actual FTF table -- fhSetValueAsRichText(ptr, rt) where rt:SetText(s, true) and s contains ' cell | cell | ... ... ' (see ftf-paragraph-formatting for the full syntax) -- not as a header line and a data line joined with bullet characters (e.g. 'When and Where born • Name if any • Sex • ...' followed by a second line of matching values). The bullet-separated form isn't FTF's own bullet markup (that's a leading '*' at the start of a paragraph, one bullet per paragraph, per ftf-paragraph-formatting) -- it's just a literal '•' character typed inline between values, which flattens the table's structure into something that reads as near-identical prose once GetPlainText() is applied (see run-lua-get-plain-text-from-richtext), making it easy to mistake a real table for a duplicate paragraph or vice versa when inspecting a record's plain-text rendering. If a source's transcription is already sitting in this bullet-flattened form and needs correcting, don't retype the certificate data by hand (transcription-error risk on live genealogy records) -- transform the existing header/data lines programmatically instead, e.g. headerLine:gsub('•', '|') and dataLine:gsub('•', '|') to build the cells directly from the text that's already there, then wrap with the header and footer.

title: Resolving a source's populated template fields: use fhGetMetafieldShortcut (or fhBridge.getPopulatedTemplateFields), not a raw-tag walk or positional match -- works on citations too
source: issue #67 (bug found: describe_project's sourceTemplateFields census always returned {}) and issue #73 (fix extracted into bridge/sourceHelper.lua's fhBridge.getPopulatedTemplateFields, shared with findSources); live-verified against a real ~4000-Individual project's actual SOUR/_SRCT data; citation-level fix and fhGetMetafieldShortcut/fhGetMetafieldType/fhGetMetafieldDefinition discovery from fh-help-corpus, live-verified against a real citation (a Civil Registration Index entry) whose populated fields resolve correctly the same shortcut way as record-level fields
text:
Two obvious ways to read a templated Source record's own populated field values both fail, live-confirmed against real (non-bridge-authored) data -- reach for fhBridge.getPopulatedTemplateFields(sourPtr) instead, or its underlying technique if you need something the helper doesn't cover.

FAILS: matching a populated field by its own raw tag. A field's definition (FDEF, child of the _SRCT template record) carries the field's CODE, but the *populated value* on the SOUR record itself is a child item whose own fhGetTag() is always the literal string "_FIELD" -- not the field's CODE, not its ~PREFIX-CODE shortcut, and with no child of its own to read a code back from. Every "_FIELD"-tagged child looks identical from the tag alone. (bridge/sourceHelper.lua's own findSources briefly assumed the opposite -- that a populated field's tag would be its ~PREFIX-CODE shortcut, matching what this bridge's own createSourceFromTemplate happens to produce when it creates one -- but that's an artifact of how this bridge's *own* write path names things, not what real FH-UI-created data (or any other plugin's writes) actually produce; fixed issue #73.)

FAILS: matching a SOUR record's Nth _FIELD child positionally against its template's Nth FDEF definition (in FDEF order). Looks reasonable since _FIELD children are created in template field order -- but breaks the moment a field partway through a source's field list is left unpopulated, since FH doesn't create a placeholder for a skipped field: every later field's position silently shifts down by one. Live-verified against a real "Civil Registration Certificate" source: template FDEF order is Type, Region, Principal, Principal_2, Date, Location, Address, Reference, Repository, Collection, URL, but Reference was left unpopulated, so the source's 8th (and last) _FIELD child actually holds Repository's value, not Reference's.

WORKS: resolve each field directly by its own ~PREFIX-CODE shortcut Data Reference (see data-references-syntax) -- FH's own field-addressing mechanism, not a positional or tag-based guess: fhGetItemText(sourPtr, "~.~" .. prefix .. "-" .. code), e.g. fhGetItemText(sourPtr, "~.~TX-Reference"). Correctly resolves to "" for an unpopulated field without disturbing any other field's answer, and (live-confirmed) formats a Date-typed field's value as display text ("11 September 1901"), not a raw internal value. PREFIX is the field's TYPE mapped via the fixed 8-entry table in source-template-creating-a-templated-source (Text=TX, Name=NM, Place=PL, Address=AD, Enum=EN, Date=DT, Repository=RP, URL=UL).

In practice, don't hand-roll this -- fhBridge.getPopulatedTemplateFields(sourPtr) (bridge/sourceHelper.lua, read-only, both Session modes, accepts a live pointer or a qualified id string) already does exactly this: resolves sourPtr's linked _SRCT template, walks its FDEF definitions, and returns {code = value} for every record-level field that resolves non-empty. Record-level fields only -- a Citation-specific field (FDEF's own CITN child, see source-template-fields) is populated per-citation, not on the SOUR record itself, so it never shows up here even when populated on some citation; whether the same raw-tag pitfall applies to citation-level fields is still unconfirmed (issue #73) -- no project data was found with an actual populated citation-level template field to test against.

UPDATE (issue #73, second pass): FH's plugin API has three purpose-built functions for exactly this that are more robust than hand-building a "~PREFIX-CODE" string from a maintained TYPE->prefix table -- found in fh-help-corpus, not something to reverse-engineer. fhGetMetafieldShortcut(ptr) takes a metafield item OR a metafield *definition* item (an FDEF, i.e. within a Source Template record) and returns the exact shortcut FH itself would use, tilde included -- live-confirmed the real form is uppercased on the code portion ("~TX-REFERENCE", not "~TX-Reference") even though Data Reference resolution turned out to be case-insensitive there so the hand-built mixed-case form still worked; fhGetMetafieldType(ptr) takes a metafield item and returns strVarType, strCode directly (both empty strings if ptr isn't a metafield) -- an alternative way to identify/enumerate populated fields by walking a record's own children, without needing the template at all; fhGetMetafieldDefinition(ptr) takes a metafield item and returns a pointer to its FDEF in the associated template (null if orphaned or not a metafield). bridge/sourceHelper.lua's shortcutFor now delegates to fhGetMetafieldShortcut(fdefPtr) rather than a hand-built prefix table.

The citation-level gap this entry originally left open IS the same bug as record-level: live-verified against a real populated citation (a "Civil Registration Index" citation with Name_on_Index/Date/Registration_District/Registration_Reference/Additional all populated) that its fields carry the same generic "_FIELD" raw tag as record-level ones, resolvable by fhGetMetafieldType(child) or by the same ~PREFIX-CODE shortcut Data Reference used for record-level fields -- just resolved relative to the citation's own live pointer instead of the SOUR record's. bridge/sourceHelper.lua's findSources now retains each citation's live pointer while walking (collectCitations rewritten to walk the live tree directly rather than a pre-built getAllDetails JSON tree, which can't carry a live pointer at all) and resolves citation-level fieldFilters the identical way as record-level, through one shared matchesFilters function.

title: fhBridge.getFamilyGroup(indiPtr, type)
source: bridge/familyHelper.lua:222-295 (issue #62)
text:
Returns every parent/sibling/spouse relationship for an Individual. Read-only, wired into both access modes.

Parameters:

indiPtr — live Item Pointer to an Individual record, or a qualified id string (e.g. "I219")

type — one of "all" (default), "parents", "siblings", "spouses"

Returns: array of {relationship, individual, family}. relationship is "father"/"mother"/"sibling"/"spouse", read off the FAMC/FAMS record's own HUSB/WIFE role rather than the parent's SEX field. family identifies which FAMC/FAMS record the relationship came through, so full siblings/a remarriage can be told apart from half-siblings/a different marriage by comparing .family.id. Deduplicated by relationship + record id; never includes indiPtr itself.

title: fhBridge.getAncestors(indiPtr, maxGenerations, dnaLine)
source: bridge/familyHelper.lua:308-391 (issue #78, docs/adr/0021-blood-relation-filter-shared-by-ancestors-and-descendants.md)
text:
Breadth-first walk up every FAMC record from indiPtr, one generation per hop. Read-only, wired into both access modes.

Parameters:

indiPtr — live Item Pointer or qualified id string; must resolve to an Individual

maxGenerations — optional cap on how far up to walk; nil/omit for unlimited

dnaLine — optional "y-chrom"/"mtdna"/"blood"; filters the result to ancestors sharing that DNA line with indiPtr, via FH's own DnaShareYChrom/DnaShareMtDna/DnaBloodRelation builtins (fhCallBuiltInFunction), not reimplemented locally

Returns: array of {generation, line, individual, family}. line is an array of "father"/"mother" steps from indiPtr down to that ancestor (e.g. {"mother", "father"} is the maternal grandfather), left unresolved to an English title. Deduplicated by pedigree collapse — each ancestor reported once, at the shallowest generation reachable.

title: fhBridge.getDescendants(indiPtr, maxGenerations, dnaLine)
source: bridge/familyHelper.lua:393-493 (issue #64, #78, docs/adr/0016-getdescendants-defers-dna-line-logic-to-fh-builtin.md, docs/adr/0021)
text:
The mirror image of getAncestors: breadth-first walk down every FAMS/CHIL record from indiPtr. Read-only, wired into both access modes.

Parameters:

indiPtr — live Item Pointer or qualified id string; must resolve to an Individual

maxGenerations — optional cap; nil/omit for unlimited

dnaLine — optional "y-chrom"/"mtdna"/"blood"; same DNA-builtin-backed filter as getAncestors. Does not support FH's "half-blood" test — a direct descendant is never half-blood per FH's own docs

Returns: array of {generation, line, individual, family}. line is "son"/"daughter" steps read off each step's own SEX ("child" when SEX is unrecorded), not "father"/"mother" role labels — a CHIL item carries no equivalent role of its own. Deduplicated by pedigree collapse, same as getAncestors.

title: fhBridge.getAllDetails(ptr)
source: bridge/familyHelper.lua:579-596 (issue #62)
text:
Recursively describes ptr and every child item beneath it as one plain JSON-safe tree. Read-only, wired into both access modes.

Parameters:

ptr — live Item Pointer — a whole record (any type, not just Individuals) or a single field/Fact item already positioned by the caller — or a qualified id string (e.g. "I219", "S1191", "F13") for a whole-record lookup; a qualified id has no way to address a sub-field

Returns: {tag, value?, link?, children?} recursively — value for items that store one, link (a descriptor of the linked record) for link-classed items, children for every child item beneath. Richtext fields resolve via GetPlainText(), not raw FTF markup. Never a raw Item Pointer.

title: fhBridge.getFactsByTag(ptr, tags)
source: bridge/familyHelper.lua:598-637 (issue #62)
text:
Filters ptr's own direct (1st-level) children down to ones matching tags. Read-only, wired into both access modes.

Parameters:

ptr — live Item Pointer or qualified id string; any record type, not just Individuals — MARR/DIV live on FAM records

tags — a single tag string (e.g. "CENS") or array of tag strings (e.g. {"BIRT", "DEAT"}); FH's exact, case-sensitive resolved tag, including custom-fact tags like "_ATTR-REGIMENT"

Returns: array, one getAllDetails-shape tree per matching child, in record order — not deduped, so a repeated tag (multiple CENS entries, a Rejected + Preferred BIRT) is fully surfaced. Empty array (not an error) when nothing matches; errors only on a null pointer or a missing/malformed tags argument.

title: fhBridge.searchByName(forename, surname)
source: bridge/familyHelper.lua:639-682 (issue #62)
text:
Finds every Individual whose given name(s) contain forename and whose surname contains surname, both case-insensitive substring (not exact/whole-word) matches against the NAME field's GIVEN_ALL/SURNAME Data Reference qualifiers. Read-only, wired into both access modes.

Parameters:

forename — optional string; omit or "" to skip filtering on it

surname — optional string; omit or "" to skip filtering on it. At least one of forename/surname must be given a non-empty value, or this errors

Returns: array of indiDescriptor ({id, qualifiedId, name, sex}), in FH's own record order (creation order, not sorted). Scans every Individual record in the project once — fine for an interactive lookup, not meant for a tight loop.

title: fhBridge.createSourceFromTemplate(templateNameOrId, fields, transcription)
source: bridge/sourceHelper.lua:423-451 (issue #18, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-30-createSourceFromTemplate-design.md)
text:
Creates a fully populated templated Source (SOUR record plus its _SRCT template link) in one call, instead of hand-assembling the link + metafield-shortcut dance. Read-write only. Validates every field against the template before creating anything, so a bad call never leaves a partial record behind.

Parameters:

templateNameOrId — the Source template's name (title, matched exactly) or its numeric record id

fields — optional {code = value} table, one entry per record-level template field to populate; Date fields take fhNewDate(...) or a {sYear[, sMonth[, sDay[, subtype]]]} table shorthand, Repository fields take an Item Pointer, everything else a plain string. Errors on a field code the template doesn't define

transcription — optional string, written as the new Source's TEXT field via FH rich text

Returns: {id, title} for the created Source record.

title: fhBridge.citeSource(ptrTarget, sourceNameOrId, fields)
source: bridge/sourceHelper.lua:512-538 (issue #99, docs/adr/0006-cite-every-fact-a-source-supports.md)
text:
Attaches a SOUR citation to ptrTarget, resolving the source by id or by title. Read-write only. Validates the target, the source, and every fields entry before creating anything, so a bad call never leaves a stray citation behind.

Parameters:

ptrTarget — live Item Pointer to an INDI/FAM record (a Whole-record citation) or a Fact item already positioned by the caller (a Fact-level citation)

sourceNameOrId — the Source record's title (matched exactly) or its numeric record id

fields — optional {code = value} table: standard citation fields (Page, Assessment, EntryDate, Text) plus, when the resolved source is templated, its own citation-specific (CITN) field codes. A reserved standard-field name always wins over a same-named template CITN field code, rejected outright rather than silently misrouted

Returns: the created citation's own live Item Pointer (not a qualifiedId — a citation is a child item, not a standalone record), so a caller can keep working on it directly (e.g. authoring FTF Text) within the same run_lua call.

title: fhBridge.getPopulatedTemplateFields(sourPtr)
source: bridge/sourceHelper.lua:599-642 (issue #73, docs/adr/0017)
text:
Returns every record-level (non-citation) templated field currently populated on sourPtr, resolved to display text. Read-only, wired into both access modes.

Parameters:

sourPtr — live Item Pointer or qualified id string for a Source record

Returns: {code = value}. Empty table (not an error) if sourPtr is a real record that just isn't templated; sourPtr being null is still a caller-mistake error, not that case. Citation-specific (CITN) fields never appear here — they're populated per-citation, not on the SOUR record itself; see findSources for the citation-level equivalent.

title: fhBridge.findSources(templateNameOrId, fieldFilters)
source: bridge/sourceHelper.lua:700-773 (issue #65)
text:
Finds every SOUR record linked to a given Source template whose populated fields match fieldFilters. Read-only, wired into both access modes.

Parameters:

templateNameOrId — the Source template's name or numeric record id

fieldFilters — optional {code = matchValue} table; case-insensitive substring match for Text/Name/Place/Address/URL fields, exact match for Enum/Date/Repository fields. Whether a field code is checked against the source record's own fields or against its citations' fields is decided per field by the template's own CITN flag, not by the caller — a citation-level filter matches if ANY of its citations has a matching value. Errors on a field code the template doesn't define at all

Returns: array of {source: <getAllDetails-shape tree for the SOUR record>, citedBy: array of {tag, qualifiedId} for every fact/record project-wide that cites it}. citedBy is unconditional (present with or without fieldFilters), so a caller can see how a template is actually used without a second helper call.

title: fhBridge.getTemplateFieldCensus(templateNameOrId)
source: bridge/sourceHelper.lua:774-844 (issue #74, docs/adr/0017)
text:
Returns occurrence counts for one Source template's fields, across the whole project. Read-only, wired into both access modes.

Parameters:

templateNameOrId — the Source template's name or numeric record id

Returns: {recordFields = {code = countOfSourRecordsPopulated}, citationFields = {code = countOfCitationsPopulated}}. citationFields counts individual citations, not distinct sources. Every field the template defines appears with a count (0 if genuinely unpopulated), distinguishing that from "not a field on this template" (which still errors, same as findSources/createSourceFromTemplate). Only pays for the whole-project citation walk when the template actually has a citation-level field to count.

title: fhBridge.logActivity(ptrRecord, action, media)
source: bridge/sessionLogHelper.lua:32-148 (issue #36, #39, #95)
text:
Logs a Session's record-creating activity into one Research Note (_RNOT) per Session: the first call in a Session creates the note, later calls in the same Session append to it. Read-write only.

Parameters:

ptrRecord — live Item Pointer to the record this activity concerns; a live FTF record link (RichText:AddRecordLink) is appended, not plain text

action — non-empty string describing what happened

media — optional {name, location} table for media the user still needs to add by hand once the Session ends; when given, appends an indented "[ ] #ToDo Media to be added <name>" sub-line (plain FTF text, not an interactive checkbox), with location in parentheses when mentioned. Never touches the media file's bytes or the filesystem

Returns: nothing — writes to the Session's Research Note as a side effect.

title: run_lua guidance: RichText:SetText's tblRecLinks parameter cannot introduce new record links -- AddRecordLink on a live/persistent object is the actual pattern (proven by sessionLogHelper.lua)
source: live-tested twice against a real project, issue #106; contradicts the literal reading of SetText.htm's own tblRecLinks parameter description and worked round-trip example; corrected pattern confirmed by reading bridge/sessionLogHelper.lua's own working logActivity implementation, which has appended record links reliably across hundreds of calls
text:
SetText.htm documents `rt:SetText(strText[, bRich[, bTFTF[, tblRecLinks[, tblCitations]]]])` as though `tblRecLinks` is a general way to supply a fresh record-links table alongside hand-authored `<rec=N,"text",auto>` tags in strText -- and its own worked example is a round-trip: GetText() an existing field to get back `sText, bRich, tblRecLinks, tblCitations`, edit sText, call SetText(sText, bRich, false, tblRecLinks, tblCitations) with that same table passed straight back. In practice this ONLY works for that exact passthrough case -- the table completely unmodified from what GetText() just returned, with no new <rec=N,...> tags added and none removed/renumbered. Live-tested twice (issue #106), both scenarios below returned false (not an error -- a silent, checkable failure if you test the return value, but a silent no-op producing plain text with no link at all if you don't):

1. A brand-new fhNewRichText() object, text containing one <rec=1,"Name",auto> tag, tblRecLinks = {somePtr} (correctly shaped: 1 entry, non-null pointer, matching the one referenced index, correct 4-arg call). Returns false every time.
2. An EXISTING rich-text field's own GetText()-returned table, extended by appending 2 new entries at the end (tblRecLinks[#tblRecLinks+1] = newPtr, twice) with 2 matching new <rec=N,...> tags added to the text -- otherwise exactly the doc's own round-trip shape, just with 2 new entries instead of zero. Also returns false every time.

Root cause, confirmed by reading a genuinely working example in this same codebase: bridge/sessionLogHelper.lua's fhBridge.logActivity keeps a MODULE-LEVEL RichText object (`buffer`) that persists in memory across every run_lua call for the whole Session's lifetime (Lua's require() module caching -- the Bridge plugin is one continuously-running Lua process per Session), and grows it purely via `buffer:AddText(...)` / `buffer:AddRecordLink(ptrRecord)` calls directly on that SAME live object, flushing with `fhSetValueAsRichText(textPtr, buffer)` each call -- it never round-trips through GetText()/SetText() at all. The record-links table is not a plain Lua array a caller is meant to freely construct or extend; it's an internal handle owned and managed BY the RichText object itself, and AddRecordLink (ftf_syntax.htm's own "FTF Record Link Syntax" section: "you cannot create a record link just by inserting text... you must use the AddRecordLink method") is the only sanctioned way to grow it -- true even when a tblRecLinks table is also supplied to SetText, not just for plain AddText.

Practical pattern for adding a NEW record link to a field that already has links (unlike logActivity's own case, which is always writing to a brand-new Session-local note): fetch the live object once with `local rt = fhGetValueAsRichText(textPtr)`, then call `rt:AddText(...)`/`rt:AddRecordLink(ptr[, strDisplayText])` directly on that SAME fetched rt (never GetText() it into a plain string+table first) before flushing with `fhSetValueAsRichText(textPtr, rt)`. The limitation this doesn't solve: AddText/AddRecordLink only append to the END of rt's current content -- inserting a link mid-document (e.g. a sub-bullet under a specific existing checklist line partway through a large field) isn't achievable this way without first calling `rt:Empty()` and rebuilding the whole field's content back up via a sequence of AddText/AddRecordLink calls in order -- and whether Empty() preserves rt's own internal record-links table or discards it along with the content is UNCONFIRMED/untested; verify this narrowly (e.g. Empty() then re-add one already-known-good <rec=1,...> reference and check GetText() still resolves it) before relying on it for a real edit, rather than assuming either way. If a mid-document insertion with a genuinely new link is too invasive or too risky to verify safely, plain text (no live link) for the new content is the confirmed-safe fallback -- no SetText/tblRecLinks or Empty() risk involved at all, at the cost of losing the auto-updating-title convenience a real record link gives.

title: run_lua guidance: editing IN THE MIDDLE of an existing large RichText field is an open problem, not a solved one
source: E40 source-transcription session, issue #107 -- surfaced as an explicitly unsolved problem (not a live-tested fix, unlike the sibling entries in this family), recorded so a future session doesn't re-attempt the same failed/untested approaches from scratch. Record-link resolution added 2026-08-15 grilling session, docs/adr/0025.
text:
Ticking a checklist box or adding a sub-bullet inside a large existing RichText field (tens of KB, hundreds of record links) means editing content IN THE MIDDLE of it, not appending to the end. Two approaches are known NOT to be simply available:

1. A full-document rewrite via rt:SetText(sText, bRich, false, tblRecLinks) with a hand-extended tblRecLinks table -- proven broken (run-lua-guidance-settext-reclinks-cannot-add-new-links, issue #106): any table beyond an unmodified passthrough of the same field's own last GetText() result returns false silently.
2. rt:AddText(...)/rt:AddRecordLink(...) on a live-fetched RichText object (the fix for #106) -- only appends to the END of the object's current content, so it cannot reach a specific existing line partway through a large field.

Suspected but UNCONFIRMED, needs empirical testing before relying on it: rt:Empty() the live object, then rebuild its entire content from scratch via a sequence of rt:AddText(...)/rt:AddRecordLink(...) calls in order -- the same way a brand-new document is built -- inserting the new ticked/linked content at the right point in that rebuild sequence rather than editing in place. Open question this hasn't answered yet: whether Empty() preserves the object's own internal record-links table (so an existing <rec=N,...> tag's link keeps resolving to the same target after the rebuild) or discards it along with the visible text -- if it discards it, every existing record link in the field would need re-adding via AddRecordLink in the same pass, not just the new one.

Before attempting this on a real, valuable field: verify it first in a throwaway, low-stakes context (a scratch record with a couple of existing record links) -- Empty(), rebuild via Add* calls including one re-adding an original link, then confirm GetText() still resolves both the old and new links correctly. Only proceed to a real field once that's confirmed safe. Until then, prefer asking the user to do checklist-style ticking by hand in FH's own UI, and use run_lua only for the underlying record writes -- fhBridge.logActivity already gives a reliable, working audit trail of what was actually done each Session, independent of any checklist text.

SOLVED for the record-link case (2026-08-15 grilling session, issue #107, docs/adr/0025-tftf-full-rewrite-for-mid-document-richtext-edit.md): see run-lua-guidance-tftf-full-document-rewrite below, live-verified twice -- once against hand-rolled script logic, once against the real fhBridge.getTftfText/fhBridge.setTftfText sandboxed functions themselves, both times against Family Historian Sample Project 8. RichText:SetText(text, true, true) (tFTF) needs no side table at all, so a full-document rewrite via it structurally cannot hit the #106 bug two paragraphs above -- fhBridge.setTftfText is a working alternative to the Empty()-then-rebuild approach above it, and moots that paragraph's own open question about whether Empty() preserves the record-links table (this technique never calls Empty() at all). Still open: a citation-bearing field's interior -- tFTF cannot represent citations at all, and silently discards one with no error if the field already has one (see the entry below) -- so this resolution covers record links only.

title: run_lua guidance: fhBridge.getTftfText/setTftfText -- editing IN THE MIDDLE of a RichText field's record links, via a full-document tFTF rewrite
source: 2026-08-15 grilling session, issue #107, docs/adr/0025-tftf-full-rewrite-for-mid-document-richtext-edit.md -- live-verified twice against Family Historian Sample Project 8: once with hand-rolled script logic exercising RichText:SetText(text, true, true)/GetText() directly, once against the real fhBridge.getTftfText/fhBridge.setTftfText sandboxed functions end to end (splice + citation guard + real write/reload persistence)
text:
fhBridge.getTftfText(ptr) fetches a rich-text field's content and rewrites every index-based <rec=N,...> reference (eFTF, as GetText() itself returns) into a self-contained <rec=QualifiedId,...> one (tFTF, resolved via fhGetQualifiedRecordId) -- safe to splice/reorder/insert into anywhere with ordinary Lua string operations (string.find(text, anchor, 1, true) for a literal, non-pattern anchor -- a bare '*'/'.'/'-' in an anchor string silently misbehaves as a Lua pattern otherwise, confirmed live during this design session), including inserting a brand-new <rec=QualifiedId,...> tag mid-document. fhBridge.setTftfText(ptr, text) commits the edited string back in one full-document RichText:SetText(text, true, true) rewrite. Because tFTF needs no companion tblRecLinks table at all, this structurally cannot hit run-lua-guidance-settext-reclinks-cannot-add-new-links's #106 bug -- there is no table to break. Live-verified: a two-record-link document, rebuilt with a new link spliced into the middle and one existing link reused a second time, round-tripped correctly through a real fhSetValueAsRichText write and a fresh fhGetValueAsRichText re-read -- the reused link deduped to one table entry, matching FH's own documented behavior, and the newly inserted link resolved correctly too.

Citation guard (issue #107's real footgun, not a hypothetical one): tFTF cannot represent source citations at all -- FH's own documented limit, not this project's -- and, confirmed live, RichText:SetText(text, true, true) does NOT error on text containing a <cit=N> marker. It silently accepts it; the marker becomes dead literal text and the citation is gone with no warning. Both functions refuse outright whenever the target field's own GetText() reports any embedded citations: getTftfText returns { text, editable = false, reason }; setTftfText re-checks at write time (in case a citation was added by hand in FH's own UI between a getTftfText call and the matching setTftfText) and errors, confirmed live to leave the field completely untouched rather than partially written. There is currently no known citation-safe equivalent -- editing a citation-bearing field's interior remains the one part of run-lua-guidance-mid-document-richtext-edit-unconfirmed that is still genuinely open; use eFTF/AddCitation directly for citation work, or ask the user to edit that field by hand in FH.

title: fhBridge.getTftfText(ptr)
source: bridge/richTextHelper.lua:75-93 (issue #107, issue #108, docs/adr/0025-tftf-full-rewrite-for-mid-document-richtext-edit.md)
text:
Fetches ptr's rich-text content as a self-contained tFTF string, safe to splice/reorder/insert into anywhere with ordinary Lua string operations (including a brand-new record link mid-document), ready for setTftfText. Read-only, wired into both access modes.

Parameters:

ptr — live Item Pointer to the rich-text field to read (a Notes field, Source TEXT, citation DATA/TEXT, etc.) — not a qualified id string; a rich-text field is a sub-record item, not a whole record

Returns: {text, editable, reason?}. editable is false — with reason explaining why, and text still returned for inspection — whenever the field has any embedded source citations, since tFTF cannot represent them and rewriting via setTftfText would silently discard them. Every index-based <rec=N,...> reference GetText() itself returns is rewritten to a self-contained <rec=QualifiedId,...> one, resolved via fhGetQualifiedRecordId; a Null linked pointer (its target record since deleted) is left as its original numeric index rather than guessed at.

title: fhBridge.setTftfText(ptr, text)
source: bridge/richTextHelper.lua:108-134 (issue #107, issue #108, docs/adr/0025-tftf-full-rewrite-for-mid-document-richtext-edit.md)
text:
Commits text (self-contained tFTF, as returned by getTftfText and then edited) as ptr's new rich-text value in one full-document rewrite — RichText:SetText(text, true, true), which needs no side table at all and so cannot hit the tblRecLinks bug documented in run-lua-guidance-settext-reclinks-cannot-add-new-links. Read-write only.

Parameters:

ptr — live Item Pointer to the rich-text field to write — same field getTftfText was called on

text — a tFTF string; record links use <rec=QualifiedId,"DisplayText",auto|text> directly, no companion table needed

Returns: none. Refuses (errors, writing nothing) if ptr's field already has any embedded source citations — re-checked at write time even if getTftfText already reported editable=true earlier, in case a citation was added by hand in FH's own UI in between. tFTF cannot represent citations at all, and SetText(text, true, true) does not error on a <cit=N> marker in text — it silently discards it — so this refusal is the only protection against that loss.

title: run_lua guidance: a `committed: true` write result only means the call didn't error -- read the field back and diff it against the intended string
source: E40 source-transcription session, root-caused against the live tool output (see e40-handoff.md's gotchas section) -- distinct from run-lua-guidance-dont-mix-writes-and-verification-in-one-script, which is about the rollback tracker, not content correctness
text: `committed: true` in a run_lua write response means the RichText/SetText/etc. call did not raise an error -- it says nothing about whether the content that actually landed on the field matches what was intended. A write can commit cleanly and still be wrong: composing a long field's content inline in a tool call risks an artifact from an unrelated, earlier tool output in the same conversation (e.g. a display-truncation marker like `[...918ch elided...]`) getting copied into the literal string being written, with nothing about the call itself failing or warning -- confirmed live, this landed verbatim in a Source's TEXT field and was accepted and committed clean. The only reliable check is a separate read-only run_lua call afterward (per run-lua-guidance-dont-mix-writes-and-verification-in-one-script) that fetches the field's current value and does an explicit equality check against the intended string, not just an IsNotNull()/length spot-check. When composing long field content, build it in a scratch/eval step first so it becomes a real string value handled programmatically, rather than hand-retyped or copy-pasted through a tool-output transcript where truncation/elision markers can appear.

title: run_lua guidance: getTftfText/setTftfText render `<rec=...>` links by QualifiedId, not by the numeral a prior RichText:GetText() call showed you -- a tick/edit script matching on that numeral will silently find nothing
breadcrumb: tFTF record-link rendering vs indexed GetText
source: E40 source-transcription session, issue #107, same investigation as run-lua-guidance-tftf-full-document-rewrite/fhbridge-gettftftext -- confirmed live on E40 checklist item 20, same field, same moment: `<rec=20,...>` via plain RichText:GetText(), `<rec=S38,...>` via getTftfText, for the identical link
text: fhBridge.getTftfText(ptr) rewrites every index-based <rec=N,...> reference (the form RichText:GetText() itself returns, N being a positional index into that field's own tblRecLinks table) into a self-contained <rec=QualifiedId,...> one (e.g. <rec=S38,...>), per run-lua-guidance-tftf-full-document-rewrite. A script that reads a record-link's numeral from a separate, earlier RichText:GetText() call (or from a prior conversation/handoff note) and then tries to locate that same link inside text obtained via getTftfText by pattern-matching the numeral (e.g. string.find(text, '<rec=' .. tostring(n) ..
